x.ASV: Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the grain.

nt: A **muzzle** is a device put over an animal’s mouth to prevent it from eating, and **threshing** is the process of separating grain from its stalks by having an animal walk on it or pull a heavy object over it. If your readers would not be familiar with these practices, you could use more general terms or explain them in a footnote. Alternate translation: [You shall not put a covering over an ox’s mouth while it is separating grain] or [You shall not prevent an ox from eating while it is trampling the grain]

Alternate translation: [will be considered the son of his dead uncle] or [will legally represent his dead uncle’s family line]

Here Moses is speaking of a man’s name as if it were an inscription that could be **wiped out**. He means that people would no longer remember that man as part of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and his name will not disappear from Israel] or [and his name will not be forgotten in Israel]

If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [God will not let his name disappear]

Here, **name** represents the person’s family line continued through his descendants. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [his memory] or [his line of descendants]

The actions **take off his sandal from his foot and spit in his face** were symbolic actions by which the widow showed that her brother-in-law would not receive any of his brother’s property because he had refused to fulfill his duty and was bringing shame on himself and his brother’s house. Here Moses is speaking of having children and continuing a family line as if it were **building up a house**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [does not continue his brother’s family line] or [does not provide descendants for his brother]

The term **and say** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly. Alternate translation: [And she shall respond]

x.ASV: Thou shalt not have in thy bag diverse weights, a great and a small.
x.Darby: Thou shalt not have in thy bag divers weights, a great and a small.
x.KJV: Thou shalt not have in thy bag divers weights, a great and a small.
x.YLT: `Thou hast not in thy bag a stone and a stone, a great and a small.

nt: Moses is using **a stone and a stone** as a common expression of his culture to refer to two different stones of different weights, **a large and a small**, used for weighing goods. This refers to a **stone** people used as a standard weight. Merchants could deceive and cheat their customers by using stones of different weights that he pretends are the same. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [unequal weights]

x.ASV: Thou shalt not have in thy house diverse measures, a great and a small.
x.Darby: Thou shalt not have in thy house divers ephahs, a great and a small.
x.KJV: Thou shalt not have in thine house divers measures, a great and a small.

nt: Moses is using **an ephah and an ephah** as a common expression of his culture to refer to two different measurements, **a large and a small**, used for measuring amounts of grain. The **ephah** was a standard measure for weighing grain. This is referring to different measurements that someone pretends are the same in order to deceive and cheat someone else. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [unequal measurements]

Here, **so that** marks God’s promise of long life as the goal or purpose of having honest weights and measures. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [in order to live many years]
